title: Product Engineering Lead
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work — and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions — because you've earned it, not because of the title.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions — and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — you'll run the technical side of it.

Most of your time stays in the code: you ship every week and own the specs, architecture, and reviews on our biggest projects. As the team grows, you'll take on 1:1s, growth conversations, and eventually managing the team.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Technical interviews and mentoring now; 1:1s, growth conversations, and the EM role as we grow.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: You've led at least 2-3 major projects from spec to production. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've taken over 1:1s as the team grew, and you're ready to step into the EM role.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've led a team technically and made it ship faster. You've set its technical direction, run its design reviews, and interviewed for it — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record. You're a senior or staff engineer whose code and designs others build on — and you want to grow into managing, not escape coding.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations in code reviews and design discussions.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer at senior or staff level, including 1+ years as a tech lead (formal or de facto) for a team of 3+

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You lead system design, not just contribute to it: you write the spec, own the architecture, and drive it to production

  • Strong OOP fundamentals; Java Spring Boot, Hibernate, or equivalent

  • Relational database design and SQL optimisation

  • Experience interviewing engineering candidates

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • Some people management and technical interviewing experience

  • Designed a technical interview process from scratch

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 60 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

  • Own the quality of compliance content in the platform (including creating policies, automated checks, evidence templates, Compliance enable playbooks for our CSMs, security awareness trainings and more)

  • Collaborate closely with CS, Product, and Founders to align compliance, customer, and roadmap priorities

  • Strong ownership mindset: operates as an individual contributor without waiting for direction

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent hands-on technical experience.

Bonus points for:

title: IT Support Spezialist –  Telematikinfrastruktur & Praxissicherheit (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Mission:

Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Kund:innen ihre IT-Systeme und die Telematikinfrastruktur im Praxisalltag zuverlässig nutzen können. Im 1st- und 2nd-Level-Support analysierst du Störungen, findest Lösungen und bist kompetente Ansprechperson rund um TI, Praxissicherheit und IT-Infrastruktur.

Dabei arbeitest du von unserem Standort in Magdeburg aus: Support und technische Unterstützung erfolgen telefonisch und per Fernwartung – Einsätze direkt bei unseren Kund vor Ort gehören nicht zu deinem Arbeitsalltag.

  • 1st- & 2nd-Level-Support: Du bearbeitest technische Anfragen telefonisch, per E-Mail und über unser Ticketsystem.
  • Fehleranalyse & Problemlösung: Du analysierst Störungen in Hard- und Softwareumgebungen und sorgst für eine zuverlässige Behebung.
  • Telematikinfrastruktur: Du unterstützt bei Einrichtung, Betrieb und Fehlerbehebung von TI-Komponenten wie Konnektoren, Kartenterminals, SMC-B-Karten oder eHBA.
  • IT-Infrastruktur: Du betreust Windows-basierte Clients, Peripheriegeräte, Netzwerke und medizinische Fachsoftware.
  • Systemchecks: Du prüfst Systeme und Infrastruktur regelmäßig und erkennst mögliche Störungen frühzeitig.
  • Installation & Rollouts: Du unterstützt bei der Einrichtung von Arbeitsplatzsystemen sowie bei Software-Rollouts und Migrationen.
  • Dokumentation: Du hältst Supportfälle und Lösungen nachvollziehbar im Ticketsystem fest.
  • IT-Sicherheit: Du achtest auf die Einhaltung unserer Datenschutz- und IT-Sicherheitsstandards und arbeitest bei Bedarf mit externen Dienstleistern zusammen.

Das bringst du mit:

  • Abgeschlossene IT-Ausbildung, z. B. als Fachinformatiker für Systemintegration, IT-Systemelektroniker oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation
  • Mindestens zwei Jahre Berufserfahrung im 1st- und 2nd-Level-Support
  • Erfahrung im Gesundheitswesen
  • Gute Kenntnisse in Windows-Client- und Serverumgebungen
  • Kenntnisse in Netzwerktechnologien und -protokollen wie LAN/WLAN, TCP/IP, DNS und DHCP
  • Erfahrung im Umgang mit Routern, Switches und Firewalls
  • Kenntnisse in Active Directory und Microsoft 365
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Ticketsystemen und Fernwartungstools
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf C1-/C2-Niveau
  • Besonders freuen wir uns, wenn du bereits Erfahrung mit der Telematikinfrastruktur oder dem Thema Praxissicherheit mitbringst.

Das zeichnet dich aus:

  • Du gehst technischen Problemen gern auf den Grund und gibst dich nicht mit der erstbesten Antwort zufrieden. Gleichzeitig weißt du, dass guter IT-Support auch gute Kommunikation bedeutet.
  • Du arbeitest selbstständig, zuverlässig und lösungsorientiert, bleibst auch bei anspruchsvollen Supportfällen ruhig und erklärst technische Zusammenhänge verständlich. Teamarbeit und ein professioneller Umgang mit unseren Kund sind für dich selbstverständlich.

Wichtig zu wissen:

  • Die Rolle ist bewusst für erfahrene IT-Fachkräfte mit Bezug zum Gesundheitswesen vorgesehen und nicht als Quereinstieg konzipiert.
  • Da du mit unserer technischen Infrastruktur arbeitest und unsere Kund:innen direkt unterstützt, findet die Tätigkeit vor Ort in Magdeburg statt.

Warum die HASOMED-Unternehmensgruppe?

  • Weil funktionierende IT im Gesundheitswesen entscheidend dafür ist, dass Praxen sich auf das konzentrieren können, worauf es wirklich ankommt: ihre Patient.
  • Bei uns verbindest du dein IT-Know-how mit einem Umfeld, in dem zuverlässige Technik und sichere digitale Versorgung unmittelbar zusammengehören.

Wir bieten dir:

  • Ein Arbeitsumfeld, das inspiriert: Unser modernes Gebäude bietet Freiflächen für kreatives Arbeiten, mobile Arbeitsplätze, einen Fitnessraum und ein „Little Office“ für Kids.

title: Senior Embedded (ARM) Engineer - Quantum Computing (m/w/d)
description:
eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Quantum computing is a new computing paradigm rapidly approaching commercial viability. Our unique approach combines laser-cooled trapped ions with microwave control and tailored magnetic fields. Our next-generation computing machines under development will be able to find solutions to problems that are out of reach today, thus enabling new innovative products and services for a brighter future.

We are looking for a Senior Embedded (ARM) Engineer (m/f/d) to join us in Hamburg or Siegen and own the real-time firmware that turns our control electronics into a working quantum computer. You will work on our next-generation system, where the control electronics are being integrated into a single, highly integrated chip. You sit at the heart of the machine, between the hardware that generates the pulses and the higher-level software that describes the experiments. Timing is not a detail here; it is the product. You are the person who makes sure the right signal reaches the ions at the right nanosecond, reliably, run after run. 

Responsibilities:

  • Own the embedded firmware on our ARM-based control platform, from architecture through implementation to on-hardware debugging

  • Develop and maintain the real-time software layer that coordinates pulse sequencing, timing, and data flow across our highly integrated control chip

  • Write and maintain the low-level drivers and board support the hardware relies on

  • Guarantee deterministic, low-latency behaviour under hard real-time constraints

  • Lead firmware bring-up together with our electronics and physics teams, and debug at the boundary where software meets signal

  • Define the firmware architecture and engineering practices — build, test, and release processes for the embedded layer as the system matures

  • Contribute to the interfaces between the embedded layer and the rest of the stack, so experiments defined in software run correctly on the machine


Required Skills:

  • 5+ years of professional embedded software development for real-time or timing-critical systems

  • Deep command of C (and ideally C++) on ARM platforms, working close to the hardware

  • Experience with bare-metal and/or RTOS environments, and a clear understanding of when each is appropriate

  • Comfortable reading schematics and datasheets, and debugging real hardware with oscilloscopes, logic analysers, and JTAG

  • Strong grasp of real-time concepts: interrupts, DMA, timing, concurrency, and determinism

  • A track record of bringing up firmware on new hardware, not only maintaining existing systems

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with experimental physicists and engineers, and to turn imprecise physical requirements into robust firmware

  • Strong adaptability and a quick learning mindset

  • Good proficiency in English (written and spoken)

Nice to have (Bonus)

  • Experience on highly integrated SoCs, particularly ARM+FPGA platforms such as Xilinx Zynq / RFSoC

  • Working alongside FPGA/digital-electronics engineers at the software–gateware boundary

  • Rust for embedded systems

  • Embedded Linux on ARM (Cortex-A), including driver and kernel-module work

  • Signal processing or control-loop implementation on embedded targets

  • Experience with high-speed data acquisition or precision timing systems

  • Familiarity with laboratory, scientific, or measurement instrumentation

  • Prior experience with quantum computing or other deep-tech domains

description:
Who are we

At Lokalise, we make it easy and profitable for businesses to expand into new markets. Our AI-powered localization platform helps companies manage both software and marketing content from a single, unified environment — ensuring every team speaks with one voice across every language and channel.

By automating workflows, integrating with over 60 tools, and centralizing translation memory and terminology, Lokalise enables product, engineering, and marketing teams to collaborate without friction and launch globally up to 10× faster and at 80% lower cost.

Trusted by thousands of businesses across more than 100 countries, Lokalise empowers millions of people worldwide to use digital services in their native languages. Backed by a customer-loved support team, our platform fits seamlessly into your design, development, and content workflows, helping you scale with consistency and control.

Location

While our company operates exclusively on a remote basis, you must reside and have the legal right to work in one of the following countries: the United Kingdom, Latvia, or Spain.

This is a full-time, remote position. Please note that we do not engage on a B2B or contractor basis.

 

About the Team

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a cross-functional team in our Product Engineering organization. Each of our engineering teams owns a product domain at Lokalise, from vision to delivery. Teams talk to customers, find out what they need, set their own goals and choose how to solve the problems that matter most.

AI is already part of how we build software at Lokalise, and it's changing what great engineering leadership looks like. We're looking for a leader who stays close to the work and understands how AI is changing speed, quality and engineers' day-to-day experience. You'll keep your teams focused on outcomes that matter to our customers and our business, not just on how much gets shipped.

For this role, you'll lead our Editing Experience team. The team owns the tools linguists and reviewers use every day to translate, review and approve content at scale: the translation editor, the review and approval workflow, content management tools and the developer utilities that support them. Together with your Product Manager and Designer, you'll own the team's strategy and delivery end to end.

 

What You Will Do

  • Lead, coach and develop your teams of Software Engineers. You'll support their career growth, run performance evaluations, contribute to compensation planning and hire engineers who raise the bar.
  • Stay technically close to the work without becoming a bottleneck. You'll review key designs and pull requests, pair with engineers on tricky problems and take on contributions outside the critical path (such as tooling, prototypes or small fixes). This keeps you in touch with the codebase and your teams' daily reality while they own delivery.
  • Partner with Product Managers and Designers (the Product Triad) to understand our customers deeply and take part in discovery. You'll make sure your teams work on the right problems, putting outcomes ahead of outputs.
  • Connect engineering decisions to business impact. Understand how your domain contributes to customer value, retention and revenue, and use that to guide trade-offs on scope, investment and technical debt.
  • Own your teams' flow of work from start to finish. Track and act on delivery and quality signals (such as cycle time, deployment frequency, change failure rate and recovery time), clear bottlenecks across planning, review, testing and release, and keep cognitive load sustainable.
  • Lead your teams' move to AI-native engineering across the SDLC. Embed AI tools and agentic workflows, measure their real effect on speed, quality and how engineers experience their work, and adapt team practices so faster delivery never costs reliability or maintainability.
  • Champion operational excellence. Drive reliability and quality practices, own the health of the services your teams run and step in as Incident Commander when needed.
  • Own your teams' delivery: set quarterly plans, track progress against the product roadmap and help shape department-wide planning and strategy.

 

What You Must Have

  • 3+ years of recent experience as an Engineering Manager leading software engineering teams, ideally in SaaS product companies.
  • A strong software engineering background, and you're still hands-on today. You can review code and designs credibly, dig into technical issues and contribute to architecture decisions.
  • Proven people leadership: hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management and helping engineers grow into their next role.
  • A strong product engineering mindset. You've partnered with Product and Design on discovery, worked directly with customers and measured success by customer and business outcomes rather than output.
  • Business acumen. You understand the commercial context, can explain trade-offs in terms of impact and communicate clearly with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Experience using engineering metrics and flow practices (such as DORA metrics, cycle time or WIP limits) to find bottlenecks and improve delivery, quality and team health, without turning metrics into targets.
  • Hands-on experience using AI-assisted development and agentic tools, both in your own work and across a team. You have a clear view of how AI changes delivery speed, code quality, review practices and cognitive load.
  • Experience planning and delivering complex initiatives across several teams predictably, including managing dependencies, risks and incidents.

 

It's a Plus If You Have

None of these are required, and we're happy to support you as you learn them on the job.

  • Experience in the localization industry or with translation workflows.
  • Experience leading engineering teams at a product company during a scale-up phase.
  • Experience shipping AI-powered product features, such as LLM-based features, to customers.
  • Experience managing fully remote, distributed teams.
  • Familiarity with developer experience or productivity frameworks, such as SPACE or DevEx.

 

Our Benefits

💰 Competitive salary and employee stock options.
🌍 Fully remote setup with flexible working hours.
🏢 Co-working budget — for those days you want a change from your home office.
🌴 Flexible vacation policy to recharge when you need to.
🖥️ Home office setup budget — monitor, desk, ergonomics, whatever helps you do your best work.
📚 Learning & development budget to grow your skills and career.
🏥 Health insurance to keep you covered.
🧘 Wellness allowance to support your mental and physical well-being.
🤝 Great startup culture — remote but close-knit, with regular retreats and social events to stay connected.

We are committed to a culture of inclusion and equal opportunities. Therefore, we welcome applications from people of all gender identities, sexual orientations, personal expressions, relationship, marital, or civil partnership statuses, racial identities, national or ethnic origins, religious beliefs, ages, and disability statuses.

title: Regional Sales Director, Strategic Enterprise - UK
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's UK Enterprise business is one of our fastest-growing segments globally. We've scaled rapidly over the past several years — consistently outpacing the broader business — and we're now at an inflection point where we need to pair that momentum with operational rigour to sustain growth at scale. 

This Regional Sales Director role is central to that next chapter. You'll lead a team of six Senior Enterprise Account Executives and Client Directors selling into some of the UK's largest and most complex organisations, spanning transportation, logistics, infrastructure, utilities, and field services. 

The team is performing — but we want to turn strong results into a repeatable, scalable engine. That means bringing structure, coaching discipline, and a proven enterprise playbook without losing the pace and builder energy that got us here.

In this role, you will: 

  • Own the performance, development, and day-to-day leadership of a team of Senior Enterprise AEs, driving net new logo acquisition and expansion across a defined set of strategic UK accounts
  • Coach your team through complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles where average contract values regularly reach seven figures over multi-year terms
  • Build and run a structured operating rhythm - pipeline reviews, deal inspection, forecasting discipline - while getting close enough to the detail to add value at the deal level
  • Develop your reps' ability to access economic buyers, build multi-threaded relationships, and position Samsara's expanding product portfolio against a customer's most critical business priorities
  • Pressure-test deal qualification, challenge assumptions, and help your team navigate the complexity of selling into large UK enterprises - this isn't a role where you sit above the deals
  • Build the commercial muscles - cross-sell, multi-product attach, stakeholder mapping - that will drive durable growth as we expand our footprint across the UK's largest accounts
  • Partner closely with the AVP of Strategic and Enterprise Sales UK, your peer RSDs, and cross-functional teams including Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Marketing to ensure your team has the support it needs to win
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
  • Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Proven experience as a frontline or second-line sales leader in B2B enterprise technology, with direct responsibility for team quota attainment
  • Track record of coaching Account Executives through complex, multi-quarter sales cycles with average deal sizes of £250K+ ACV, but with experience of seven figure ACV deals 
  • Experience selling into large, multi-stakeholder organisations where procurement, legal, and multiple business units are involved in the buying decision
  • Demonstrated ability to build and enforce a structured sales operating cadence — pipeline generation, deal qualification, forecasting accuracy, and stage progression
  • Strong commercial instinct for multi-product or platform selling, where the value proposition spans multiple use cases and buyer personas

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience at a high-growth technology company that was scaling its enterprise go-to-market in the UK or EMEA — ideally where you helped build or refine the playbook rather than inheriting an established one
  • A coaching-first leadership style with a track record of developing AEs from good to exceptional, not just managing top performers
  • Experience managing forecast accuracy as a discipline, not just an output — particularly in an environment where leadership investment decisions depend on the reliability of your calls
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, scaling organisation where not everything is perfectly defined yet, and where you're expected to build process while delivering results
  • A blend of strategic thinking and tactical intensity — you can set a multi-year account strategy and also jump into a deal review and tell a rep exactly where their qualification is weak

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in ----- ----- or ----- For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

title: Founding Engineer - Ambient Care Startup
description:
Stage: Pre-seed. Location: Cambridge/London, UK. Comp: Competitive + Equity

About Subtle

Most families find out something's wrong too late: a fall, a missed check-in, a change no one noticed until it became a crisis. We're building ambient sensing for the elderly and vulnerable at home, technology that quietly looks out for the people we love without asking them to wear anything or change how they live. We're early. We're validating with real customers, building the first hardware, and looking for the person who'll help turn this from an idea into a product families can trust with something this personal.

We are building this from scratch inside Founders Factory's studio, with a dedicated pre-seed investment, hands-on studio support across product, design, talent and growth, and a six-month build programme to get from concept to a fundable, in-market product. This venture has secured a major European technology partner. The founding CEO is already in place. We are now looking for the technical other half of the founding team.


The role

You'll be our first engineering hire, working directly with the founder(s) and carrying real authority over what we build and how. It's a hands-on role that spans hardware and software, and a leadership one too, since you'll grow the team that follows you.

Responsibilities

  • Own hardware validation and bench testing end to end, and lead our manufacturing path. Whether that ends up being an outsourced partner or in-house, you're the one validating the sensor platform yourself and making sure whatever we ship has been properly tested before it reaches someone's home. This is safety-relevant, so you'd rather catch a failure on the bench than have it happen in someone's home.

  • Build the software that turns sensor data into something useful. Detection logic, alerting, and the escalation decisions that sit behind them, tested and monitored with the same rigor as the hardware.

  • Navigate the regulatory and security requirements that come with this territory. Certification requirements for embedded systems (software and hardware), and data protection for Personally Identifiable Information (PII), from day one rather than retrofitted later.

  • Grow the team. As we scale past this hire, you'll hire, mentor and lead the engineers who join under you.

What we're looking for

Must have's

  • Early-stage hardware experience. You've taken a hardware product from 0 to 1 in a startup environment, and you're comfortable spanning embedded systems and software.

  • Experience using AI to accelerate how you work, across engineering, prototyping, and the day-to-day operations of running a startup.

  • Experience leading or building a small engineering team, or clearly ready to step into that.

  • A proactive, evidence-first way of working. You're comfortable with ambiguity, and comfortable being told (including by yourself) that a result doesn't hold up.

  • Experience with regulatory, security, or compliance requirements in health tech, medical devices, or another safety- and privacy-regulated space. You understand that building for vulnerable people and their data changes what "done" means.

  • Lead vendor and manufacturing negotiations, securing the right partners, terms, and production capabilities to bring the product to market.

  • Any direct experience taking a regulated product through certification (CE/UKCA, FDA, or equivalent) is considered a major plus.

title: Risk & Control Manager
description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for a Risk Manager to join our Risk & Control team, part of Pleo's Second Line of Defence. You'll report to our Head of Risk and Control, helping build and run our enterprise risk management framework, from risk appetite linkage through to the risk reporting our senior leaders and committees rely on. Alongside that full ERM remit, you'll own second line oversight of security, technology and operational resilience risk, giving our technology and security teams informed, credible challenge. It's a rare mix: a broad enterprise risk role with a technology risk specialism, in a FinTech that's still shaping how it manages risk as it scales. We value people from a range of risk backgrounds, so if you match most of what's below, we'd love to hear from you.

Who you'll be working with and reporting to

You'll report to our Head of Risk and Control, who leads Pleo's second line risk function and our enterprise risk management framework. You'll work closely with our Assurance & Controls Manager on testing, our Credit & Product Risk Officer, and the security GRC team in the First Line, as well as teams across Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and Compliance.

What you’ll be doing

As a Risk Manager, you will:

  • Build and run our ERM framework: Act as deputy to the Head of Risk and Control on our enterprise risk management framework, including risk appetite, how it links to our risks and controls, and the reporting that goes to senior management and governance committees.

  • Own technology and security risk oversight: Lead 2LOD oversight of information security, technology and operational resilience risk, setting the methodology and standards and challenging the First Line on where the gaps are.

  • Test our IT general controls: Run ITGC testing with our technology and security teams, assessing whether controls are well designed and working in practice.

  • Lead high-risk testing when incidents happen: Partner with our Assurance & Controls Manager to lead incident-driven testing in our highest-risk areas and turn findings into clear actions.

  • Run risk assessments and RCSAs: Lead risk assessments and risk and control self-assessments across the business, not just in technology.

  • Shape our GRC tooling: Run pilots of GRC tools and help decide how we bring more structure and automation to how we manage risk.

  • Be a trusted risk partner: Advise First Line teams on risk, regulatory change and the control environment, and support our engagement with regulators.

Right now we're broadening what the team covers. We already have strong financial and credit risk skills in the team. This hire closes our gap in technology risk and gives us a second person who can run enterprise risk management end to end. You'll work across a risk universe that spans technology, information security, privacy and operational resilience, alongside product, operational and financial risk.

What you bring

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Enterprise risk management depth: Hands-on experience running an ERM or operational risk framework in a regulated financial services business (FinTech, banking, payments or similar), including risk appetite, risk reporting and RCSAs. You could step in for the Head of Risk and Control when needed.

  • Technology risk know-how: Hands-on experience applying security, technology and operational resilience risk methodology and standards, with enough depth to challenge technology and security teams credibly. You don't need to be an engineer.

  • Controls testing experience: A track record of ITGC testing or similar control testing and assurance work.

  • The ability to influence: Confidence engaging stakeholders on complex or sensitive risk topics, challenging constructively and being heard.

  • Clear, collaborative communication: The ability to translate risk concepts into practical language for everyone from engineers to senior leadership.

  • A pragmatic mindset: A drive to find workable answers to real risk challenges rather than defaulting to theory.

Nice to have:

  • First Line experience, for example in an IT, security or GRC team before moving into second line risk

  • Experience with GRC tooling, including selecting or rolling out a platform

  • Exposure to data risk or AI risk

  • Experience at both a FinTech and a traditional bank or payments business


How you’ll develop in this role
In your first 12 months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Get under the skin of Pleo's risk landscape and take ownership of key 2LOD review and challenge activities across priority business areas.

  • Play an active role in evolving our risk framework as the company continues to scale — contributing your expertise to initiatives that will shape how we manage risk for years to come.

  • Build strong relationships across the business, establishing yourself as a credible and trusted voice on risk matters.

We're committed to helping you grow here, whether that means deepening your technical expertise, expanding your regulatory knowledge, or stepping into broader leadership responsibilities as the team develops.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You've run enterprise or operational risk frameworks and want to go deeper on technology and security risk

  • You started in IT, security or technology risk and have since moved into broad, enterprise-wide risk management

  • You enjoy building and improving frameworks in a scaling business, and want to be a genuine deputy to the head of the function

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • Your experience is mainly First Line security or GRC work without broad enterprise risk management. This role covers the whole risk universe, not just technology

  • Your background is primarily consultancy, internal audit or compliance without substantial hands-on risk and control experience

  • You want a mature, settled framework to maintain. A lot of this role is building, testing and piloting while the business moves around you

How you'll develop in this role

In your first 12 months at Pleo, you'll:

  • Take ownership of key ERM framework deliverables alongside the Head of Risk and Control, including risk appetite linkage and committee reporting

  • Set our technology and operational resilience risk methodology and complete a full cycle of ITGC testing

  • Run a GRC tooling pilot through to a clear recommendation on how we manage risk at scale

As deputy to the head of the function, you'll get broad exposure to senior stakeholders and governance, with room to grow into wider leadership as the team develops.

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  • Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  • Hiring manager interview: A conversation with our Head of Risk and Control.

  • Peer interview: A conversation with two members of our Risk & Control team.

  • Final interview: A conversation with our Chief Risk Officer.

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25+ days of holiday + your public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we're looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a Risk Manager, we received a lot of applications but only meet with a select few. With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it's a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the "Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z" formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you've worked on. title: Senior Data Product Partner - (Spend & Control)
description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

The Opportunity:

We are building a new team of Data Product Partners to bridge the gap between business needs and complex data systems, ensuring our data assets are trustworthy, discoverable, impactful and truly solve user problems.

As a Senior Data Product Partner (DPP), you will be the driving force behind the impact of our data team with the Perk business. You will move fluently between business and data worlds, making critical decisions rooted in both user needs and technical reality. Your goal is to move beyond simply providing solutions to proving demonstrable business impact.

  • Role Title: Senior Data Product Partner

  • Reporting To: Manager, Data Product Partner

  • Core Mandate: Be the primary data consultant, fixer, strategist, and relationship manager for a specific business domain (e.g. Customer Care, Finance, Marketing, Revenue, Spend & Control, Travel)

  • We are open to either Regular or Senior profiles

What You’ll Do:

Relationship Management and Strategy

  • Develop Business Data Strategy: Collaborate with business leaders to define how data can drive their strategic goals, solve critical challenges, and uncover new opportunities

  • Identify and Qualify Value: Proactively identify high-impact use cases and data initiatives that will generate maximum measurable value (e.g., revenue increase, cost reduction, efficiency gain) for the partner business unit

  • Act as the primary translator across all disciplines, explaining the same concept differently to different data team roles and executives

  • Proactively manage expectations and define the appropriate scope and flexible roadmaps

  • Develop Product Sense for Data, anticipating common data quality issues, recognising when simpler solutions are better, and strategically saying "no" to requests that compromise our aligned vision

  • Publicise and amplify the work that has been done to drive adoption of and learning from our solutions

  • Coach teams to be able to self serve their own preliminary investigations

Demand Shaping and Portfolio Management

  • Focus on defining what to build and why (Data Product Partner) rather than how (AE/ DA/ DE/ DS/ DG). Ensuring that we built the right thing - vs the Data Team Lead owning did we build the thing right

  • While the Data teams own the timeline estimates, the DPP defines the urgency, the required business target date and the prioritisation, which then influences how the Craft team approaches the estimate

  • Shape and Prioritise Demand: Work with business stakeholders to clarify their data needs, translating vague requests into well-defined, measurable projects and technical data requirements that can be handed over to the Data Teams

  • Manage the Business Unit's Data Portfolio: Oversee the pipeline of data projects, data products and initiatives relevant to their business unit, ensuring alignment with capacity and strategic priorities. Work closely with Data teams to evaluate technical tradeoffs with potential business impact

  • Conduct Value Realisation Tracking: Continuously monitor and report on the actual business outcomes and ROI delivered by completed data projects and products

Ad-Hoc Analysis, Triage & Intake Management

  • The Data Product Partner is the first line of response for data questions from the business and plays a critical role in determining the right level of effort and ownership

  • Conduct initial ad-hoc analysis where appropriate, including lightweight SQL queries, exploratory analysis in Looker as well as quick validations, sanity checks, and hypothesis testing

  • Use this initial analysis to answer simple, time-sensitive business questions directly, clarify the underlying problem and assess feasibility, data quality, and potential impact

  • Triage and prioritise ad-hoc requests by determining whether the request can be resolved quickly vs. requires deeper analytical or engineering work. Escalate and hand over well-defined requests to Data Analytics, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science or Data Governance when needed. Provide clear context, urgency, and success criteria to downstream teams

  • Actively identify recurring ad-hoc requests that indicate a gap in existing dashboards or data products, a need for improved data quality, documentation, or enablement or an opportunity to convert reactive work into scalable data products

Consultation and Enablement

  • Provide Data Consulting: Offer expert advice to business stakeholders on data availability, appropriate methodologies, and the interpretation of data insights

  • Drive Data Literacy and Adoption: Champion the use of data tools and insights within the business unit, coaching teams on how to effectively integrate data into their daily decision-making processes

  • Proactively surface observations, trends, or risks as nuggets of insight

  • Bridge the Data-to-Action Gap: Ensure that insights are clearly communicated, translated and embedded into concrete business actions and process changes

  • Ensure that the pain points of Data Quality gaps are identified and prioritised within the Data Team

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

Quantum Dot Process & Characterisation Engineer- Post-Growth Processing (Master)
description:
Quandela stands as a global leader in quantum computing, driven by groundbreaking technology and a strategic vision for scaling quantum solutions. The company’s unique ability to offer both hardware and software solutions, along with its commitment to build energy efficient datacenters and scalability, positions it to play a key role in the next wave of innovation, and in many strategic and sovereign industrial sectors. 

Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀

Role overview

We are looking for a Process & Characterisation Engineer to prepare and validate GaAs/AlGaAs samples containing InAs quantum dots (QDs) through the first steps of our single-photon source fabrication flow.

The role combines hands-on cleanroom processing – chemical treatment, PECVD deposition and high-temperature annealing – with optical characterisation of the QDs before and after each step. The data you produce decides whether a sample is ready to move forward, and how the process recipes should be adjusted.

You will start by running an established, well-documented procedure with rigour and consistency. As you build expertise, the role is designed to grow: within your first year, you will contribute to optimising the process, automating the measurement setups and taking ownership of sample validation for these steps, working closely with both the Production and R&D teams.

Sample preparation & processing (from day one)

  • Run the established step-by-step procedure for preparing GaAs/AlGaAs samples with InAs quantum dots.
  • Carry out the cleanroom fabrication steps: chemical surface treatment, PECVD deposition and high-temperature annealing.
  • Follow recipes and operating procedures precisely, and flag any deviation, drift or anomaly as soon as it appears.
  • Contribute to a safe, disciplined and efficient cleanroom environment.

Optical characterisation & validation

  • Measure QD optical properties before and after processing, using photoluminescence and white-field imaging, including at cryogenic temperature.
  • Compare pre- and post-processing results against acceptance criteria to decide whether each sample can be released to the next fabrication steps.
  • Adjust process recipes based on measurement results, within defined process windows.

Data, reporting & traceability

  • Analyse measurement data using Python and report results clearly and regularly to the Production and R&D teams.
  • Maintain the sample database so that every sample’s processing history and measurements are fully traceable.
  • Keep process documentation and procedures up to date.

Growing your scope (within the first year)

  • Contribute to the automation and optimisation of the optical measurement setups and data-acquisition pipeline.
  • Propose, design and test improvements to the fabrication steps, using experimental data and the scientific literature.
  • Take ownership of sample validation for these steps, including defining checks and acceptance criteria.
  • Contribute to the development and qualification of new or additional process steps, together with the R&D team.

Requirements

Required qualifications & experience

  • Master’s degree (Bac+5) in Materials Science, Semiconductor Physics, Optics, Micro/Nanofabrication or a related field.
  • Solid foundations in semiconductor physics, particularly III-V materials.
  • Solid foundations in optics and in semiconductor fabrication processes.
  • Fluency in Python for data analysis.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a rigorous approach to experimental work.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to investigate technical problems using experimental data and scientific literature.
  • Clear documentation and communication skills.
  • Fluent English, both written and spoken.

Preferred qualifications

  • Hands-on cleanroom experience, ideally in III-V device fabrication: wet and dry etching, PECVD deposition, thermal processing.
  • Hands-on experience with optical characterisation, including building and aligning optical setups (photoluminescence, white-field imaging).
  • Experience with cryogenic measurements (e.g. 40 K Stirling cryostat).
  • Experience automating instruments or measurement setups with Python.

You enjoy hands-on work in the cleanroom and the lab every day, and you get satisfaction from a measurement done right and a sample that is fully traceable. You are comfortable applying an established procedure with rigour, and curious enough to ask why a result looks the way it does.

Over time, you want to do more than follow the recipe: you are ready to propose ideas, make decisions based on experimental results and modify the process accordingly. You are autonomous, proactive, and enjoy working at the interface between Production and R&D.

If you are passionate about semiconductor fabrication and quantum technologies, we would love to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every box.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience
  • Profit-sharing & company savings plan
  • 100% health coverage (Alan)
  • 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
  • Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
  • Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer:

  • A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
  • A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
  • Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

Process

      1. Talent Acquisition interview (30–45 minutes).
      2. Hiring Manager interview (45 minutes).
      3. Technical interview and team meeting.
      4. Two reference checks.
      5. Offer.

title: Photonics Packaging & Cryogenic Integration R&D Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry.
Its offerings include a very energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers.
Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components.
Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Description of the Team/Project

We are looking for a Photonics Packaging & Cryogenic Integration Engineer to contribute to the development and industrialization of our photonic quantum systems.

You will work on the integration of single-photon sources, photonic integrated circuits and optical/electromechanical assemblies, with a strong focus on miniaturization, automation and operation under cryogenic conditions.

This is a highly hands-on role at the intersection of photonics, electronics, mechanics, automation and experimental physics.

You will contribute across the full development cycle: design, prototyping, assembly, testing, optimization and transfer toward industrial-scale production.

Your Key Responsibilities: 

    • Design and develop packaging and integration solutions for photonic and quantum devices.
    • Integrate single-photon sources, photonic integrated circuits and optical components into complete systems.
    • Develop and optimize optical coupling strategies, including fiber coupling and direct chip-to-chip integration.
    • Design, build and assemble precision positioning and alignment systems, including nano-positioning stages and multi-axis platforms.
    • Develop experimental setups operating under cryogenic conditions, typically in the 2–4 K range.
    • Design mechanical parts and assemblies using CAD tools.
    • Contribute to electronics development, including PCB design, instrumentation and control systems.
    • Automate alignment, test and characterization processes using Python, C++, Rust or similar programming languages.
    • Work with microcontrollers, FPGA-based systems or other hardware-control architectures when relevant.
    • Build, test and iterate rapidly on prototypes, including using 3D printing and other rapid prototyping techniques.
    • Perform test and measurement activities to characterize system performance and identify failure modes.
    • Contribute feedback to the design of photonic chips and single-photon sources based on integration and testing results.
    • Support the transition from laboratory prototypes to repeatable and scalable manufacturing processes.
    • Document designs, experiments, procedures and lessons learned, and actively share knowledge within the team.

Requirements

What we're looking for: 

You should ideally bring:

  • A PhD in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, applied physics, condensed matter physics, solid-state physics, optics, photonics or a related field.
  • Strong hands-on experience building and testing scientific or high-precision equipment.
  • Experience with photonics, optomechanics, semiconductor devices, cryogenics or precision engineering.
  • Familiarity with optical alignment, fiber coupling and/or photonic packaging.
  • Experience with mechanical design and CAD tools.
  • Good understanding of electronics, instrumentation and test equipment.
  • Programming skills in Python, C++, Rust or similar languages for automation and hardware control.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary systems combining optics, mechanics, electronics and software.
  • Strong experimental problem-solving skills and the ability to iterate quickly from concept to prototype.
  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to produce clear technical documentation and collaborate in an international environment.

Nice to Have

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

  • Cryogenic systems and experiments at very low temperatures.
  • Photonic or optoelectronic packaging.
  • Chip bonding, indium bump bonding or related micro-assembly techniques.
  • Pick-and-place systems or automated precision assembly.
  • Nano-positioning and multi-axis motion control systems.
  • Robotics or computer vision.
  • FPGA or microcontroller development.
  • PCB design using KiCad or similar tools.
  • Finite-element simulation using tools such as ANSYS or COMSOL.
  • Semiconductor or quantum photonics environments.

More than a specific academic background, we are looking for someone who enjoys building complex scientific systems and solving problems directly at the hardware level.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience
  • Company savings plan
  • 100% health coverage (Alan)
  • 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
  • Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
  • Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer:

  • A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
  • A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
  • A hybrid work model (3-4 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris or 1 to 2 days remotely)
  • Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview (30' - 45')
  • Hiring Managers Interview (45')
  • Use Case (a live use case or one to be prepared at home and presented afterward)
  • Meeting with the teams
  • 2 to 3 reference check
  • Offer

title: Product Owner WIFI, RF & Embedded Systems
description:
Chez Exotec, nous mettons l’excellence technologique au service de la redéfinition des relations entre humains et robots. A travers le monde, nos solutions révolutionnent la façon dont nos client·e·s délivrent leurs produits aux personnes consommatrices finales. Nous contribuons au succès des plus grandes marques du commerce et de l’industrie, tout en améliorant les conditions de travail de leurs salarié·e·s.

Par l’alliance de l’intelligence artificielle et d’un hardware performant, nos robots sont désormais déployés dans le monde entier et leur succès a fait de nous la première licorne industrielle française.

Rejoindre Exotec, c’est l’opportunité de donner du sens à vos compétences. Grandissez avec nos ExoPeople dans le monde entier pour faire de vos idées, des réalités.

La révolution robotique portée par Exotec ne fait que commencer, vous en êtes ?

Au sein de l'équipe Product Management ASRS, le Product Owner Connectivity est responsable de la stratégie produit, du développement, de la performance et de la fiabilité des solutions de connectivité déployées sur une flotte mondiale de plus de 12 000 robots autonomes.

Le Product Owner Connectivity pilote l'ensemble des solutions de communication sans fil utilisées au sein des systèmes robotiques et équipements associés. Il garantit leur performance, leur robustesse, leur évolutivité et leur conformité aux exigences opérationnelles et de sécurité.

À l'interface entre les équipes Software, Electrical, Safety, Architecture, Validation et Opérations, il définit la roadmap produit et assure la livraison de solutions de connectivité répondant aux besoins actuels et futurs de l'entreprise.

Missions :

Solutions de connectivité

  • Pilotage du développement et de l'évolution du nouveau module WiFi propriétaire développé en interne.
  • Pilotage des organes de sécurité utilisant des technologies RF.
  • Responsabilité des équipements électriques intégrant ces technologies de communication.
  • Définition et suivi de la stratégie de connectivité des systèmes robotiques.

Gestion produit

  • Construire et maintenir la roadmap produit Connectivity.
  • Prioriser les évolutions fonctionnelles et techniques en fonction des enjeux business et opérationnels.
  • Recueillir et challenger les besoins des parties prenantes internes.
  • Piloter les arbitrages entre performance, coût, fiabilité et délais.

Performance & fiabilité

  • Assurer la disponibilité et la robustesse des communications sans fil à grande échelle.
  • Analyser les incidents terrain et définir les plans d'amélioration continue.
  • Suivre les indicateurs de performance et de qualité des solutions déployées.
  • Garantir la scalabilité des solutions pour accompagner la croissance de la flotte.

Coordination technique

  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Embedded Software, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering et Safety.
  • Contribuer aux choix d'architecture des futures générations de produits.
  • Assurer la cohérence des solutions développées avec la stratégie technologique globale.

Profil

  • 8 à 10 ans d'expérience dans le développement de produits ou systèmes technologiques complexes, idéalement dans un environnement industriel.
  • Solides connaissances en connectivité sans fil (WiFi 5 GHz / 6 GHz, technologies RF, couverture, roaming et performance réseau).
  • Bonne compréhension des systèmes embarqués, de leurs architectures logicielles et des contraintes associées (temps réel, cybersécurité, sécurité fonctionnelle).
  • Connaissance des architectures électriques et systèmes industriels, avec la capacité à collaborer efficacement avec des experts hardware, software et systèmes.
  • Expérience du pilotage de sujets techniques complexes et de la coordination d'équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Excellentes capacités d'analyse, de résolution de problèmes, de communication et d'influence.
  • Fort intérêt pour l'innovation technologique, l'amélioration continue et les environnements industriels exigeants.

Benefits

  • Couverture mutuelle et prévoyance santé compétitive
  • Politique famille avantageuse
  • Programme de mobilité interne et internationale
  • Nombreuses opportunités de formation et de développement

Chez Exotec, nous garantissons l’égalité des chances dans notre processus de recrutement. L’ensemble des candidatures reçues sont étudiées indépendamment de l’âge, du genre, de l’origine, de la religion, de la couleur de peau, de la nationalité, du sexe, du handicap, de l’orientation sexuelle ou de toute autre distinction protégée par la loi.

Nous mettons en place un environnement de travail inclusif et respectueux de toutes les différences.

Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information: www.mirakl.com.

Mirakl in Numbers:

  • 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40
  • 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo
  • 🇫🇷 350+ Mirakl Tech teams members mainly based in France
  • ⚙️ 5 Saas Solutions

Our Values:

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

  • 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success
  • 🏆 Get Things Done:  We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results
  • 🚀 Go Above & Beyond:  We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence
  • 🎓 Succeed Through Expertise: Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture
  • 🤝 Satisfy & Empower Clients: We're committed to our clients' success

The Team You'll Join

You'll be part of our Security team within the Platform, Data & AI Security pillar, led by Maxime Lahaye, Senior Security Officer, based in Paris.

AI is fundamentally transforming how we work, and you'll join a team at the forefront of this evolution. This is your opportunity to build the GRC infrastructure of tomorrow, where automation, scripting, and security converge to enable Mirakl's next phase of growth.

This is a permanent position (CDI) based in Paris or Bordeaux, with 4 days on-site per week.

 

Your Impact

1 · Compliance & Certifications — Automation-first

  • Contribute to maintaining Mirakl's ISO 27001, ISO 27018 and SOC 2 certifications, leveraging automated GRC platforms to enable continuous compliance monitoring
  • Automate evidence collection, control monitoring and documentation workflows using modern GRC tooling, AI-powered agents and scripting (Python, N8N)
  • Help manage and evolve the ISMS (Information Security Management System), ensuring it reflects both regulatory requirements and Mirakl's evolving AI-driven operations

  • Co-design and evolve Mirakl's AI usage governance framework: acceptable use policies, data classification for AI inputs, shadow AI detection and AI vendor risk assessment
  • Maintain a live inventory of AI tools used across the company and contribute to the risk-based process for evaluating and onboarding new tools
  • Monitor the AI governance regulatory landscape and help adapt Mirakl's framework proactively

3 · Security by design across all company projects

  • Partner with Product and Engineering teams early in project lifecycles to embed security and compliance requirements from the start

What You'll Bring to the Role

Experience:

  • Master's degree (Bac+5)
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in cybersecurity
  • You participated in ISO 27001 audit as a security contributor at least
  • Proven experience in scripting and automation (Python, N8N or equivalent)
  • Experience in a consulting firm or technology company is a plus
  • Strong understanding of compliance frameworks and security standards

  • Proactive and autonomous, with strong organizational and problem-solving abilities
  • Excellent communication skills to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Integrity and ethics as core values
  • Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams

Tools Used

Languages
